we propose a novel Memory Matching Network that is trained with a few examples and learns to learn the network weights in one shot learning.
we introduce Memory Matching Networks (MmNet) for one shot image recognition.
Memory Matching Networks (1) are a novel deep architecture for one shot learning, (2) are trained with a few examples per category, and (3) are trained with minibatch learning.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MM Net is a novel deep architecture for one shot learning, which can learn from one example and generalises well.

our Memory Matching Networks (i) are the first deep architecture for one shot learning, (ii) can be trained with a few examples per category and (iii) can be trained without any prior knowledge of the number of categories and number of shots at train time.
our MM Net is able to learn a unified model for all the categories and the number of shots, which is the first time in the literature of one shot learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel deep architecture, Memory Matching Networks, that can be trained on one shot learning and is able to output a single model irrespective of the numbers of shots and classes.
MM Net could learn a unified model to perform one shot learning for a large number of new categories with only a few examples.

we have developed a deep architecture that can learn to learn the network weights for unlabelled data on the fly in a sequential manner, which is a novel idea and has never been explored in one shot learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the memory matching networks can be used to learn a model from few examples, which can then be applied to new examples.
the proposed MM Net can be trained on the fly with the unlabelled data, which is more flexible than conventional one shot learning methods.
memory matching networks could learn the parameters of a deep model in an end to end manner for the unlabel data.
